hero.title: Discover the benefits of the Korbous thermal station
hero.subtitle: Warm mineral water, ochre cliffs and the quiet of the Gulf of Tunis. For the length of a stay, the pace slows down.
hero.imageAlt: Korbous, a white village between the cliff and the Mediterranean

intro.title: A hot spring at the edge of the Mediterranean
intro.p1: Korbous is a thermal station on Cap Bon, in the Nabeul governorate. The village steps down between the hill and the Gulf of Tunis, about 51 kilometres east of the capital via Hammam Lif.
intro.p2: In publications of the Office of Thermalism, its springs are described as known since antiquity. The water linked to the station — notably that of Aïn Echfa — is a hyperthermal water dominated by sodium chloride. This site informs; it does not replace medical advice.
intro.imageAlt: Corniche and white houses of Korbous along the gulf
intro.statLabel: east of Tunis, via Hammam Lif

benefits.title: What the water of Korbous shows
benefits.intro: The points below repeat published data. They describe the water. They promise no result.

items.title: Hyperthermal water
items.text: Aïn Echfa is classified as a hyperthermal water dominated by sodium chloride, with a published temperature of 59 °C and a pH of 7.5.

items.title: Mineralisation
items.text: The published dry residue is 11,812 mg/l. Sodium and chlorides dominate, with calcium, magnesium and sulphates.

items.title: Where it meets the sea
items.text: Several springs rise at the foot of the cliffs. Aïn El Atrous, about one kilometre north of the village, flows toward the Mediterranean.

items.title: A place of care
items.text: Thermal documentation mentions a medicalised station and baths. A cure is decided with a health professional.

featured.title: Three ways to meet the water
featured.intro: A demonstration catalogue. Durations and prices are examples, in the absence of an official list published here.

facilities.title: The village, the springs, the coast

items.title: The thermal village
items.text: White houses, a corniche and an open view of the gulf: Korbous is walked as much as it receives treatments. The thermal establishment belongs to this landscape.

items.title: The springs
items.text: Aïn Echfa, Aïn Sbia, Aïn El Atrous and Aïn Kalassira are among the most often cited springs. Spellings vary slightly between publications.

items.title: The Cap Bon shore
items.text: Ochre cliffs, coves and scrub-covered hills follow the road that links the station to the sea.

gallery.title: Light, rock and water
gallery.text: Photographs of Korbous and its shore, published under free licences. Treatment rooms are not shown: we show the place as it is seen.

why.title: Three reasons to take the corniche
why.imageAlt: Sunset over a cove on the Korbous coast

items.title: Between cliff and sea
items.text: The station opens directly onto the Gulf of Tunis. The landscape is part of the stay.

items.title: Documented water
items.text: The temperature, pH and mineralisation of Aïn Echfa are published. The figures should still be confirmed with the station.

items.title: Close to Tunis
items.text: About an hour by road via Hammam Lif is enough to reach Cap Bon.

testimonials.title: Voices written to illustrate a stay
testimonials.notice: Demonstration testimonials. They do not come from real visitors and do not describe a treatment result.

items.quote: The quiet of the corniche, early in the morning, is already worth the journey. You understand the place before you even enter the water.
items.name: Leïla M.

items.quote: One day was enough to slow down: the white village, the sea just below, and a bath taken without hurry.
items.name: Marek W.

items.quote: Nothing spectacular, and that is precisely it. A shore, warm water, time.
items.name: Inès C.

location.title: Coming to Korbous
location.text: The station is on Cap Bon, in the Nabeul governorate. From Tunis, the road passes through Hammam Lif and then follows the coast.
location.address: Korbous Thermal Station, Korbous, Cap Bon, Nabeul governorate, Tunisia

about.heroText: A village on Cap Bon, hot springs, and water whose characteristics are published. What is not established is not invented.
about.heroAlt: Cliffs and Mediterranean coast near Korbous
about.lead: Korbous stands on a narrow passage between the hill and the sea. That contact — thermal water, rock, gulf — gives the station its character.

history.title: Known since antiquity
history.p1: Publications of the Office of Thermalism state that the spring of Aïn Echfa, at Korbous, was already known since the earliest antiquity.
history.p2: Travel accounts associate the site with the Latin name Aquae Calidae Carpitanae. This page does not reconstruct a chronology: dates, founders and works that are not established here are not filled in by guesswork.
history.imageAlt: White houses and minaret of Korbous on the hill

location.title: Cap Bon, facing the Gulf of Tunis
location.p: Aïn Echfa lies at a published altitude of 5 metres, 51 km east of Tunis via Hammam Lif. Korbous is in the Nabeul governorate. The corniche follows the cliffs before dropping toward the village.
location.imageAlt: Korbous seen from the coastal road, between sea and hill

water.title: Published characteristics
water.note: Figures published for Aïn Echfa. They describe a reference analysis and should be confirmed with the station.

stats.label: Classification
stats.value: Hyperthermal water dominated by sodium chloride

water.text: Official documents cite fields of treatment — rheumatology, dermatology, gynaecology — without this site turning them into promises. Medical advice comes before any cure. Aïn El Atrous, one kilometre to the north, is another hyperthermal sodium-chloride spring, with a published temperature of 58.6 °C.

nature.title: Cliffs, scrub and the Mediterranean
nature.p: The land falls to the sea in ochre cliffs. Coves, scrub and the light of the gulf make up the station’s setting. At Aïn El Atrous, hot water visibly meets the sea: where it leaves the rock, it is too hot for a direct bath.
nature.imageAlt: Cove and layered rock on the shore near Korbous
nature.secondAlt: Hills and a small cove on the Korbous coast

bain-individuel.name: Individual thermal bath
bain-individuel.summary: A quiet immersion, in a private cabin, in the station’s warm water.
bain-individuel.description: The individual bath is the simplest form of balneation: a limited time in the water, then rest. Spring water is very hot; for a treatment it is brought to a bearable temperature. This sheet shows how such a care can be presented. It sets neither a protocol nor a price.
benefits: Time away from passing traffic
Direct contact with the thermal water
A short session, easy to place in the day
bain-individuel.info: People being treated for an illness, who are pregnant, or who take medication should ask for medical advice before any session. The temperature at the spring outlet is not the temperature of the bath.

douche-thermale.name: Thermal shower
douche-thermale.summary: A jet of thermal water, often offered around the bath.
douche-thermale.description: The shower concentrates water on one area, with limited pressure and duration. It is presented here as a possible complement to the bath, in the register of classic thermal techniques. The sheet remains a demonstration.
benefits: A more local application than the bath
A brief session
A simple gesture, explained before it begins
douche-thermale.info: Pressure and temperature are set for comfort. Any skin or vascular sensitivity should be mentioned before the session. This is not a medical indication.

massage-affusion.name: Massage under affusion
massage-affusion.summary: A massage accompanied by a stream of thermal water.
massage-affusion.description: Affusion lets a stream of warm water run during the massage. The gesture stays slow. This pairing is common in thermal stations; its exact availability at Korbous, its duration and its price are to be confirmed. The sheet is an example.
benefits: The warmth of the water and the massage together
A slow pace
A relaxing session, with no therapeutic promise
characteristics: Oil or water alone, according to local practice
massage-affusion.info: Mention any area to avoid. The care illustrated here does not treat an illness.

enveloppement.name: Rest wrap
enveloppement.summary: A warm, wrapped pause after contact with the water.
enveloppement.description: The wrap extends the warmth of the bath: you stay lying down, covered, while the body settles. No specific ingredient — mud, seaweed or otherwise — is claimed here, in the absence of an official station sheet. The example describes only the principle of a warm rest.
benefits: A calm extension of the bath
Little gesture, a great deal of quiet
A transition before going back outside
characteristics: Without a product whose composition is unconfirmed
enveloppement.info: Prolonged heat does not suit everyone. If in doubt, ask for advice before booking this kind of care — from a professional, not through this site.

soin-visage.name: Facial with thermal water
soin-visage.summary: A comfort treatment for the face, using the station’s water.
soin-visage.description: Thermal water is sometimes applied gently to the face, for a moment of comfort. This sheet does not describe a dermatological treatment and names no particular cosmetic active. It shows a possible wellness session, to be confirmed on site.
benefits: A short, seated moment
A gentle application
No talk of a “skin cure”
characteristics: No promise about complexion or a skin condition
soin-visage.info: Broken skin, an ongoing dermatological treatment or a known sensitivity should be mentioned before any facial.

parcours-detente.name: Relaxation route
parcours-detente.summary: Half a day linking a bath, a pause and the shore.
parcours-detente.description: The route offered here is a demonstration sequence: a bath, a quiet interval, then a short walk to the shore if the weather allows. It is not an official package of the station. Order and duration may be quite different on site.
benefits: A simple reading of a day in Korbous
Care and landscape in the same stretch of time
No commitment to a result
characteristics: Time outdoors according to the weather
parcours-detente.info: Bring drinking water, stable shoes and something to cover yourself after the bath. Opening hours remain to be confirmed.

seance-relaxation.name: Relaxation session
seance-relaxation.summary: A guided quiet time, without a specific thermal procedure.
seance-relaxation.description: Guided relaxation is done lying down or seated, in a quiet room. It does not necessarily use thermal water. It is presented as a possible complement to a day at the station, and only as an example.
benefits: Time without a technical gesture
Slower breathing
A pause between two treatments
seance-relaxation.info: You may stop the session at any time. Nothing here constitutes psychological care.

decouverte-station.name: Discovering the station
decouverte-station.summary: An introduction to the village, the springs and how to approach the water.
decouverte-station.description: This discovery is a commented demonstration visit: the village, the idea of the springs, and the precautions around very hot water. It replaces neither an official guide nor a consultation. The exact route depends on what is open on the day.
benefits: Finding your way through the village and the shore
Understanding where the water is too hot
Asking practical questions before a treatment
decouverte-station.info: The corniche is narrow in places. A visit keeps a careful pace, especially in full sun.

practical.locationText: Korbous Thermal Station, Cap Bon, Nabeul governorate, Tunisia. Aïn Echfa lies 51 km east of Tunis via Hammam Lif, at a published altitude of 5 metres.
steps: From Tunis, head toward Hammam Lif, then take the coastal road to Korbous.
The corniche winds along the cliffs: a calm drive is more pleasant.
Public-transport lines and timetables are not reproduced here, for lack of a confirmed schedule.
useful: The water of Aïn El Atrous emerges very hot: the published temperature is about 58.6 °C. Do not bathe at the outlet.
Stable shoes help on wet rock.
Buying a voucher on this site is a demonstration: it stays in this browser and does not reserve a place.
Bring drinking water. It is separate from the spring water.

faqs.q: Can I book a treatment on this site?
faqs.a: The voucher purchase is a demonstration on this device. It sends nothing to the station and takes no payment. The contact form does not send a message either.

faqs.q: Are the prices and hours exact?
faqs.a: Not when they are marked as examples. No official price list is displayed here.
A thermal cure is prepared with a health professional. This site gives no personal indication and does not repeat the conditions listed in official documents as promises.
On the west coast of Cap Bon, in the Nabeul governorate, facing the Gulf of Tunis. Allow about 51 km from Tunis via Hammam Lif for Aïn Echfa.

faqs.q: Can you bathe at Aïn El Atrous?
faqs.a: The water where it leaves the rock is scalding. Visitors stay where it mixes with the sea, and keep away from the outlet. Care is still needed, especially with children.
